KNOWN_PREFILLS.detail: The values themselves are right: all 16 canonical and 14 boundary writes print in full and land on their own measured rules. The FAIL is that the delivered participant guide contradicts itself about one of them and misdescribes what the participant received. participant-instructions.md line 33 says the packet wrote 'your name, date of birth, case number, street address, city, state and ZIP on the proposed order'. Its later section 'What the platform deliberately left blank' then says: 'The State line at section 1 of the order. The rule Colorado draws there is 31 points wide ... and this packet writes your city and your ZIP on either side of it. Write your state on it yourself.' In the delivered canonical bytes that line is NOT blank: reports/actual-writes.json records defendant-state drawn as 'CO' at rect x 393.93 y 380.38 w 27.25, pdftotext reads 'City: Denver State: CO Zip Code: 80202', and I counted 84 added ink pixels inside that rect in the rendered page. The family's own byte proof agrees with the bytes and against the guide: blanks-left-for-the-participant.json nearMissesRefusedByRole records 'This build narrows the threshold through the module's own option, writes the state on the form's own drawn rule'. The bullet reads as a sentence left behind by the very fix build-findings.json describes (rulesOfPage minLength narrowed from 40 to 24 so this 31.25pt rule would be seen). It is unconditional, so one of the two sentences is always wrong: false for canonical, where the state is printed, and true only for the boundary case where 'Colorado' spelled out is refused as unfittable. A participant told to hand-write a state onto a proposed order that already reads 'CO' writes over correct data on the document the judge signs. Repair is in the guide generator, not in the overlay geometry: make both sentences conditional on the recorded refusal for the fixture being described.

PROTECTED_FIELDS.detail: No ink at any protected blank, proven from the rendering rather than from the field map: pages 3 of JDF 683 and 2 of JDF 686 are pixel-identical to their pinned sources, so the petitioner signature and date, the lawyer signature line, the item 14 certificate of service and its date and recipients, and the judge-or-magistrate signature and order date all carry nothing. On the two caption pages 100 percent of added ink falls inside declared write rects, so the Division and Courtroom boxes are untouched. Recorded observation, not scored as a failure: the same court-use-only block also holds the Case Number line, and the packet does write the participant's own court-assigned case number there while refusing Division and Courtroom on the strength of the same printed 'This box is for court use only' label. I do not read that as a protected write - the case number is participant-held identifying data the clerk needs to route the filing, and omitting it would be worse - but the inconsistency in the family's own reasoning is worth the Captain seeing.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: Checked by rendering, as the sibling failure requires, not by bounding boxes. The doubled-outline shape that failed co_petition_seal_arrest-set cannot arise here and does not: the delivered fixtures contain no /AcroForm, no /Widget and no /Btn token, pdf-lib reads 0 form fields, and no widget appearance is flattened because there is no widget. The stronger test is the pixel one: differencing each delivered page against its pinned source gives 0 removed pixels everywhere (nothing printed is covered) and every added pixel inside a declared write rect (0 unaccounted on all four pages that carry writes). There is no second ring anywhere, no square stamped over a printed word, and no ink at any of the 22 printed controls. Values fit their rules; the two that did not were refused rather than clipped.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Measured against the controlling record, which establishes no fee. rules.fees reads 'Unconfirmed. The fee must be confirmed before building.' and rules.feeWaiver reads 'The source review does not address a fee waiver.' Both print verbatim in both delivered guides, the packet states no amount anywhere, and its first section tells the participant to ask the municipal court clerk what the fee is and not to read the packet's silence as 'there is nothing to pay'. No fee, waiver, deadline or clerk practice is fabricated.
